28:1.sourceText: Καὶ διασωθέντες τότε ἐπέγνωμεν ὅτι Μελίτη ἡ νῆσος καλεῖται.
28:1.targetText: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

groups.note: The participle διασωθέντες ("having been brought safely through") is rendered Once … were safely ashore.
Μελίτη is the island of Malta.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous chapter and is not separately expressed.
BSB leaves τότε ("then") unexpressed; Once … already marks the sequence.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; BSB supplies we for διασωθέντες (as Acts 22:5).

28:2.targetText: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

groups.note: Same verb, in a different form in BSB's Greek text.
οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν ("not the ordinary") is rendered extraordinary, as Acts 19:11.
τὸν ἐφεστῶτα ("that had set in") is folded into BSB's it was raining.

28:27.sourceText: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μή ποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
28:27.targetText: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’

groups.note: The aorist ἤκουσαν ("they heard") is rendered with the English present they hear.
βαρέως ("heavily, with difficulty") is rendered hardly.
The article τοῖς is used as a possessive and rendered their.
μή ποτε ("lest") is rendered Otherwise.
The article τοῖς is used as a possessive and rendered their.

The singular καρδίᾳ ("heart") is rendered hearts, one for each of them.
The article τῇ is used as a possessive and rendered their.

28:28.sourceText: γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπεστάλη τοῦτο τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ· αὐτοὶ καὶ ἀκούσονται.
28:28.targetText: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”

groups.note: The imperative ἔστω ("let it be") is rendered Be.
γνωστόν ("known") is rendered advised.
The καί after αὐτοί ("they too, they indeed") is rendered and.

28:30.sourceText: Ἐνέμεινεν δὲ διετίαν ὅλην ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι, καὶ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους πρὸς αὐτόν,
28:30.targetText: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.

groups.note: διετίαν ("a period of two years") is rendered two … years.
The article with the participle τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους ("those coming in") is rendered who came.

28:31.sourceText: κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάσης παρρησίας ἀκωλύτως.
28:31.targetText: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

groups.note: μετὰ πάσης παρρησίας ("with all boldness") is rendered Boldly.
ἀκωλύτως ("unhindered") is rendered freely.
τὰ περί ("the things about") is rendered about.
